caption:
The mountain sets the pace; you decide whether to argue. When the incline steepens and the road turns to gravel, the internal noise fades until there is only the rhythm of your own breath and the persistent pull of the grade. It is not about speed. It is about staying present when your lungs begin to ask for a reason to stop. In these moments, you learn that the terrain doesn't care about your goals or your fatigue. It simply exists, waiting for you to match its quiet, relentless demand.
